issue: Does the Supreme Court's holding in Honeycutt v. United States, which limits forfeiture to property the defendant himself obtained, apply to forfeiture under 18 U.S.C. § 981(a)(1)(C)?

sides.position: Honeycutt applies to forfeiture under § 981(a)(1)(C), so a defendant can be forfeited only property he himself obtained (position not identified in the excerpts)
cases: United States v. Channon, 973 F.3d 1105, 1115 (10th Cir. 2020)

sides.position: Even if Honeycutt applies, a defendant who actually possessed or acquired the full proceeds of a criminal scheme can be held liable for those funds, including funds later transferred; under § 982(a)(1), a co-conspirator who acquired the full proceeds may be ordered to forfeit them
cases: United States v. Tanner, 942 F.3d 60, 67–68 (2d Cir. 2019)

quote: We recognize that “a circuit split has developed over whether Honeycutt applies to a forfeiture under 18 U.S.C. § 981(a)(1)(C),” which does not use any form of the word obtain.
cite: United States v. Cline, No. 24-1119 (10th Cir. 2025)
